text: MOS Bridge is a local AI-operator system for software projects with a web console, supervisor, driver loop, project channels, memory, audits, and parallel workers.
The main channel is for the bridge itself. Each external project should have its own channel with separate state, backlog, project binding, and project memory.
Runtime state, chats, backlog history, logs, uploads, worktrees, projects, auth, secrets, API keys, and local databases must not be committed to the bridge repository.
New projects should be planned deeply before execution: UX map, UI routes and states, client/server/data plan, risks, tests, and acceptance criteria.
Parallel work should be created from dependency-aware backlog atoms. Only non-conflicting atoms with clear file or domain boundaries should run in parallel.
The operator chat should show planning decisions, backlog generation, worker dispatch, verification evidence, acceptance results, and blockers.

Project memory should store durable facts, decisions, risks, tests, invariants, open questions, and worklog entries. Bridge memory can inform projects, but project memory should stay project-local unless explicitly shared.
A project can look complete while still failing real navigation, auth, profile routes, or acceptance scenarios. Final acceptance must test real user flows against the project plan.
On Windows PowerShell 5.1, .ps1 files that contain Cyrillic or emoji should be saved as UTF-8 with BOM and checked with Parser.ParseFile before restart.
Autonomy is safest when external project channels can execute backlog tasks, while the main bridge channel remains conservative by default.
